title: Six Flags Over Georgia: What we know about Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem and the fatal roller coaster incident | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

As investigators work to determine how a man fell to his death during a roller coaster ride Monday at Six Flags Over Georgia, authorities have identified the victim as abeloved educator,prompting an outpouring of grief across the Atlanta community and school system.

Cobb County Police on Tuesday identified the victim as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old man who worked at an Atlanta public charter school as its IT manager, technology teacher and robotics coach.

While few details have been released, witnesses say he fell from a hypercoaster called Goliath, a 210-second ride that reaches 70 mph and a height of 200 feet, according to the Six Flags website.

In the wake of his death, at least 10similar rides across six parksin the US and Canada have temporarily closed as investigators work to establish what happened.

Here’s what we know:

Preliminary information gathered at the scene from witnesses and employees indicated Kariem had been ejected from the ride, the Cobb County Police Department’s Major Crimes Unit said. He struck other riders before falling beneath the roller coaster, where he was found “unresponsive and not breathing” at around 4 p.m., police said in a statement.

Police did not disclose the name of the roller coaster, but witnesses described seeing the man fall from Goliath, and aerial footage reviewed by CNN showed Goliath riders stopped at a steep incline before being evacuated down a high stairway.

“He fell and hit the car three different times” before falling onto the roof of a haunted house attraction below, a witness toldCNN affiliate WXIA.

One witness told WXIA the falling man was captured on his souvenir picture taken while on the Goliath ride.

Another witness,CiCi Nelson, told CNN she was in line to ride Goliath when a cart pulled up with an empty seat and other riders in hysterics.

She said the safety bar on the empty seat appeared loose, and another young passenger appeared to be covered in blood and injured. Emergency personnel quickly arrived, and she and others were asked to evacuate the area.

One man was “freaking out, saying someone fell off” and was urging staff to call for help, CiCi Nelson added.

Joshua Nelson – no relation to the witness – told CNN he was at Six Flags with Kariem, who was engaged to Nelson’s sister. Nelson’s sister, niece and four daughters were also there to celebrate one of his daughters’ 13th birthday, he told CNN.

Joshua Nelson said he left the park with three of his four daughters earlier that afternoon, but the daughter celebrating her birthday stayed behind.

She was sitting next to Kariem when he fell from the ride, he said.

“His final moments and words were with her,” Joshua Nelson told CNN. “She called me crying after the ride ended stating Mr. Hassan fell off the ride.”

He told CNN his daughter has been “really strong and resilient” since the incident.

KeJuan Taylor, a supervisor at Six Flags, told CNN he was the first person to find Kariem where he fell.

“I have not suffered any physical injuries but it has been on my mind very recently through these past days,” he said.

Taylor added that it’s been “genuinely horrifying” trying to process the situation since he left work.

Four minors were injured in the incident, police said, but no further details about their condition will be released because of their age.

“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today,” Six Flags Over Georgia said in a statement Monday evening. “Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest’s family, friends, and loved ones.”

Detectives from the Major Crimes Unit are investigating Kariem’s death, police said, and have requested anyone with information to contact the department.

The Georgia Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire, which oversees safety inspections of amusement and carnival rides, has also launched an investigation of the roller coaster.

“Our investigative team is conducting an in-depth and comprehensive review to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and to ensure full compliance with all applicable policies and procedures,” the agency said in a statement Tuesday.

“Our very professional inspectors have inspected every one of those (roller coasters) before the park season even started, and they’re currently on the ground looking at every nook and cranny, conducting interviews and conducting a thorough review of what happened,” Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner John King said when asked about the incident during alive debate for Georgia’s Insurance Commissioner hosted by the Atlanta Press ClubTuesday.

“I look forward to be able to report back to the Georgia public that these rides are safe, they will continue to be safe, and we will continue inspecting them from top to bottom,” King said.

Kariem was a “cherished member” of Wesley International Academy, a public charter school in Atlanta, where he worked as an IT manager, technology teacher and robotics coach, Atlanta Public Schools said in a statement.

Kariem’s “presence and impact will be deeply missed by our students, staff, and all those whose lives he touched,” the school district said.

In a separate statement shared with CNNaffiliate WANF, Wesley International Academy (WIA) Executive Director Jason Marshall said the school community is “devastated by the loss of Hassan Kariem, affectionately known as Mr. Kariem, who was a beloved colleague, friend, and integral part of the Wesley family for more than 12 years.”

“Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community,” the statement read.

Two of Kariem’s former students described him as joyful, patient and an inspiration.

“He never got mad at us … He was always patient with us. He would joke with us,” former WIA student Soledad Gomez, who had Kariem as her computer lab teacher, told WANF.

Gomez told WANF Kariem inspired her to pursue a degree in elementary education, while her brother Juan Pablo Gomez told the outlet Kariem’s class sparked his interest in information technology, a subject he’s majoring in.

CNN has reached out to WIA for comment.

At least nine rides across several Six Flags parks in the US and Canada have been temporarily closed, a park spokesperson said. A ride was also closed at a former Six Flags park in Quebec. Several of those rides are categorized as hypercoasters – like Goliath –– rides made of steel with a height of more than 200 feet.

Goliath is manufactured by Bolliger & Mabillard, a Swiss company with a “stellar” safety record, according to Brian Avery, a professor at the University of Florida who specializes in ride safety and risk management.

Avery said Goliath features a waist restraint but has no over-the-shoulder harness like some other roller coasters –– a secondary restraint he believes should be considered.

“If you have your primary fail, what are you left with? Yeah, nothing,” he said. “And it’s an impossible feat to stay contained if it did fail, because of the forces, the speed.”

Bolliger & Mabillard issued a statement calling Monday’s deadly accident “tragic” and offering condolences to those affected.

The company said it is investigating but would have no further comment, “until we have a better understanding of what transpired.”

Every ride at its parks “undergoes extensive inspection and maintenance procedures,” according to Six Flags’ website.

Daily inspections are undertaken by park teams, while third parties, including state ride inspectors, insurance inspectors and engineering experts, also regularly evaluate the rides,it says.

When it comes to determining if Six Flags could be held legally liable for the death, more information is needed, saidDaniel Adamson, a personal injury attorney and managing partner at Dixon Adamson in Atlanta. Amusement parks have a duty to “exercise ordinary care” to protect their guests from harm under Georgia premise law, he said.

Negligence under that law could include things like failing to enforce height and weight requirements, failing to perform maintenance or inspections or not properly training employees, he said.

Adamson said preventability will be a key question: “what Six Flags knew or what they should have known.” Investigators will need to drill down on if the incident happened because of a mechanical failure, an operational failure, a design problem from the manufacturer, or a combination of factors, the attorney said.

Six Flags Over Georgia will open again on Friday, as scheduled, a spokesperson for the park told CNN. Goliath will remain temporarily closed.

CNN’s Julianna Bragg, Rebekah Riess, Elise Hammond, Holly Yan, Sara Smart, Meridith Edwards and Avni Trivedi contributed to this report.
